subject.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution

question: After the merged-config preactivation gap is fixed, should this PR land with lifecycle preactivation as the bootstrap boundary for explicit external-plugin heartbeat targets?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes existing bootstrap timing for explicit external-plugin heartbeat delivery, which is a compatibility and message-delivery tradeoff beyond the narrow mechanical latency bug.

options.title: Fix merged-config scan and accept lifecycle preactivation
options.body: Require preactivation to mirror the runner's effective heartbeat configs, then land with startup, reload, request, doctor, and target:last boundaries as designed.

options.title: Require broader live external-plugin proof
options.body: Ask for live startup, reload, and requested-heartbeat proof for an external plugin target before accepting the compatibility change.

options.title: Pause for another compatibility design
options.body: Keep wake-time bootstrap until maintainers choose a different boundary for external-plugin heartbeat delivery.

recommendation.title: Fix merged-config scan and accept lifecycle preactivation
recommendation.body: Require preactivation to mirror the runner's effective heartbeat configs, then land with startup, reload, request, doctor, and target:last boundaries as designed.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried and merged the prior external-plugin heartbeat bootstrap compatibility path that defines the boundary this PR changes.
